newsitem.title: UK: MMC report on TransCo unlikely before UK election. [CORRECTED 21:46 GMT]
newsitem.headline: MMC report on TransCo unlikely before UK election. [CORRECTED 21:46 GMT]

text.p: (The Department of Trade and Industry has clarified its position, making clear that the report will be published by Ofgas and may not need ministerial clearance. Headline and text corrected accordingly.)

The publication of a Monopolies and Merger Commission report on controversial proposals for a new pricing regime for gas pipeline operator TransCo, part of BG Plc, will very likely take place after the elections on May 1.

The MMC said it aims to hand over its findings to gas industry regulator Ofgas on April 13, but a watchdog spokesman said it is "very, very unlikely" Ofgas will have the report ready for release before May.
The report may have to be passed on to the Trade Secretary if people who have supplied information to the MMC request that this would not be made public, the Department of Trade and Industry said.
If such requests are made, the secretary will have to approve them within 14 days.
The MMC has been vetting Ofgas's price proposals since October after they had been rejected by BG, which was then still called British Gas.

At the time, the company argued the proposals, which seek a 20 percent cut this year in TransCo's charges to gas suppliers, would leave it with insufficient funds to maintain an efficient and reliable pipeline network.
If accepted, the price proposals would also lead to a drastic cut in BG's dividend, investors fear.
